item.title: Press "A" to Jump
item.description: A character that appears in the background of video games, corrupting it enough to drag the player into the distorted and horrific game.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): standard layout. Special Containment Procedures, description, discovery log and testing logs

Elevator Pitch:
basic idea is, there is a character that appears in video games and corrupts the game every time the player fails or loses a level/life. once corrupted enough, the character appears in the foreground and grabs the player through the screen. trapping them in the corrupted game.

Central Narrative:
The scp foundation finds this SCP by going to a POI's last known position. Who claimed to be part of GAW (gamers against weed). when they find his place one of the agents turns on a TV and is pulled into the game. When tested the game cartridge, it is found that any video game that comes within a 200-300 meter radius of the cartridge becomes infected and slowly turns into duplicate.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
this SCP is unique in the sense that people will fear dying, pausing or leaving a video incomplete. which many people do IRL, giving more spooks the people trapped inside will still be alive and suffering in a corrupt, horrific and incompatible game. only being able to communicate when some plays the game.

Additional Notes:
second try at an SCP. hope this idea is better.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: Green Man's Chefs
item.description: A mysterious restaurant named Green Man's Kitchen suddenly appeared in 19XX. The building was shutdown and destroyed but it's anomalous chefs have gone missing.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

  • Green Man's chefs are green faceless humanoids wearing a chef's attire.
  • They are sentient and are capable of speech despite without having a mouth.
  • They are extremely hostile to living things, especially humans except for their human employees.
  • They can cook anything with any substance, material, and etc. except for pure metals.
  • The non-chef employees are humans and are unaware that the chefs are anomalous.
  • The customers do not know of their existence.

Central Narrative: In 19XX, a restaurant named Green Man's Kitchen suddenly appeared in Alaska. Ever since it's appearance, sightings of faceless green chefs were reported. People that lived near the restaurant claimed that most of their possessions were stolen. Some people went missing. The restaurant had a constantly changing menu and it never showed what the ingredients were. The employees said that they've never seen the chefs and no one has seen the restaurant's kitchen. The restaurant shut down due to sanitary reasons. The restaurant was then destroyed by a wrecking ball.

Investigators found that the restaurant had used different materials as ingredients for their food. Some of the ingredients also included humans, clothes, animals, [Redacted]. The SCP Foundation only managed to capture only 6 of the chefs. It is studied that when one of them have gathered a main ingredient, a door appears and the chef enters. After 30 minutes, the chef comes out with food prepared with the ingredients it has gathered.

Tests were made with various non edible materials and the resulting dish is reported to be delicious no matter what the ingredients were and how it was prepared.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: These entities can cook anything and the tests that can be done with their ability. Figuring out how these entities came and formed a restaurant and what their origin may be.

Additional Notes: This is my first SCP. So, it might be messy or not good.

item.title: The Three Sided Coin
item.description: A coin that turns men into monsters, figuratively and literally.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article and Tales

Genre: Horror

Page Layout: Standard SCP layout, Wild West layout (think Aces and Eights style) for first tale.

Elevator Pitch

  • Its an anomalous coin that will reveal 3 different sides when flipped over. The 3rd side is anomalous.
  • When the coin lands on the 3rd side it transforms whoever flipped it into a monster.
  • In addition if someone keeps the coin for a long time it will alter their behavior, making them kinda crazy but in a fun way.

Central Narrative: The coins most interesting part isn't the monster but more so what it does to the people in possession of it. It makes them more exuberant, more fond of games and gambling, risk, chaos, but not necessarily evil. Its like the coin makes whoever is holding it chaotic neutral,
but they just happen to have a chaotic evil toy in their pocket, so they're dangerous. The tales will focused less on the coin itself but more on the people its effecting.

Hook: The characters. The concept can be used pretty easily to create stories. The idea that this coin is just floating around and anybody can have it allows people to come up with their own interpretation of how the coin might corrupt someone. Plus the monster is pretty badass too in my opinion.

Notes: I have a draft tale and a rudimentary scp article already written if anyone is interested is seeing them let me know.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: Epstein didn't kill himself
item.description: The surveillance footage from Epstein's cell is anti-memetic
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Modern events

+ show block
– hide block

Page Layout (Optional):

Special Containment Procedures: A copy of the scp is kept on hard drive kept in safe.

Description: Video is antimemetic. Foundation wants to know what happened in the video because Epstein was already on their radar for potential ties to a redacted GOI. Research with dangerous z-class mnestics was recently authorized

Document #XXXX-01: letter of authorization

Document #XXXX-02: Report on research with z class mnestics sent to O5. Contains test log with dialogue. Reveals that Epstein was murdered.

Document #XXXX-03: Internal document from O5 council. They believe that it was MC&D. Now they want to use that info to the advantage of the foundation.

Elevator Pitch: The surveillance feed of Epstein's death is anti-memetic. The SCP foundation wants to uncover the mystery of what happened as well as why it was covered up.

Central Narrative: Starting with the Description, I'm going to build a sense of an imposing conspiracy regarding Epstein's death. I will do this by hinting that Epstein was already on the Foundation's radar for being tied to a redacted GOI. I'm going to then hype up the efficacy of z-class mnestics by having their usage require authorization from the O5 council. Using Z-class mnestics as a benchmark, I'm gonna emphasize how extremely anti-memetic the footage. However, the testing will ultimately pull through and reveal that Epstein was murdered. Finally, in a post climax reveal, an internal document from the O5 council will reveal who they bbelieve murdered Epstein, tying back to the redacted GOI from earlier: Marshall, Carter, and Dark Ltd.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP focuses on modern conspiracies that I imagine everyone on the SCP wiki are familiar with (and maybe even buy into).

Additional Notes: I know that writing an article about Epstein requires care. If I make things to political, I can drive out half of the readers. I also have to make sure remain respectful to his victims. I'm aware of that responsibility and I won't post an article unless I'm confident that I satisfy both of those benchmarks.

item.title: A World Of D-Class
item.content:encoded:

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A portal to a hell of sorts that contains all evil people that have died, which the Foundation decides to use for D-Class

Central Narrative: The Foundation's use of D-Class personnel raises some questions in terms of logistics and morality, which can be limiting given the number of D-Class they supposedly go through, as compared to IRL numbers. This SCP is the challenge to the traditional notion of D-Class, with the current common notion being simply a cover in order to keep the SCP a secret

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It gives a reasonable method of providing a major part of the Foundation's required human cost.

Additional Notes: I am fairly good at Wiki Syntax, so the Top Secret nature can be made to be pretty convincing

item.title: The Man Who Snorts Video Games, Books and Movies Like Cocaine
item.description: A cokehead decides to snort more than just cocaine...
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: I have no clue

Elevator Pitch:

  • A cokehead grows ashamed of himself one day and decided to smash a few of his video games. He gets the bright idea to snort the fragments and discovers that doing so gives him a signifcantly weaker version of the main character's powers/skills/abilities/etc.
  • Example: snorting Super Mario Bros lets him jump 18 feet in the air. The catch? He'll break his ankles when he lands.
+What the heck did I just write...?
-Uhh....

Central Narrative:

  • After spending much of his life disappointing his family, friends and divorced spouse, he goes on a downward spiral and then discovers his anomalous ability.
  • At first, he tries to do good.
  • He tries to help an old lady cross the road by snorting Super Mario Bros, picking her up and jumping across the street. It doesn't end well.
  • Then he snorts Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and gets the Master Sword. He attempts to stop a bank robbery. However, he has no formal sword training and ends up dropping it, firing the Master Sword energy beam and accidentally killing someone's dog. The robbers then kick his ass and leave.
  • He finally decides to go down the road of villainy instead.
  • He snorts a copy of Megaman and tries to rob a bank. He ends up burning his hand off because it turns out human flesh isn't made to rapid fire concentrated plasma shots.
  • The Foundation finally notices him and tries to contain him.
  • He snorts a copy of Grand Theft Auto and tries to steal a car.
  • Well, he steals a car, alright.
  • He can't drive and ends up crashing into a fire hydrant.
  • The Foundation catch up to him.
  • Turns out, he kept a secret weapon all him all along; it's a little glass vial filled with fragments of a copy of Persona 5. He snorts it, magically dons a really beat up, low quality edgy black trenchcoat that smells like it hasn't been washed since Persona 1's release date.
  • He tries to summon Arsene and all he gets is a floating top hat that fires a tiny glob of darkness. All it does it make the Foundation Agent sneeze.
  • He gets contained.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Um. Well. He snorts things.

Additional Notes:

Possible copyright issues? I forgot to give a movie and book as an example. Oh well.

item.title: Amateur wizards and how to contain them
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Containment procedures, then description of the scp’s and finally interviews addendums and what the foundations future with the scp may hold

Elevator Pitch: A young man found by the foundation with limited knowledge of most anomalies involving, or labeled as magic. A modern day architect can’t explain exactly how the great pyramids were built, but can gain a basic understanding by examining them, and probably come up with a Rough theory. This scp can do the same with magical/ mythical items. As well as use any gained knowledge to concoct his own as he puts it amateur level anomalies ( can’t go into to much detail without making this to long)

Central Narrative:The article shows there interest in his ability to understand the anomalous effects of certain scps, But also the danger he can pose to himself and some people around him, due to his lack of expertise or a mentor. Containment procedures start off easy as they get to know him. But as they realize just how powerful he is the foundation gets stricter and stricter. Finally getting to foam padded rooms, and masks to prevent him from saying any incantations. And it also shows the lengths the foundation goes to in order to prevent the scp from harming itself, via failed magic something he does often. Including all the things listed above. And other things like sealing him in one part of his containment cell at a time to prevent him from gathering the materials to conduct anything. And also going to multiple lengths to prevent him from being captured by enemy forces.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The scp’s complete immaturity and lack of expertise or knowledge of just how powerful he can be, make him extremely hard to utilize in any situation. But his ability to gain an understanding on certain anomalies make him extremely useful to the foundation. If they can just keep a 14 year old “amateur witch” as he often labels himself: under control

Additional Notes: I am extremely worried about this scp being to overpowered or lacking in restriction. So if that does come up please tell me how to fix it. This whole scp is themed around a witch that’s to young to fully understand what there doing so I was thinking of adding a cat like scp companion. ( this idea will most likely be scrapped due to the already difficult task of polishing the main idea). This is my very first concept so I am fully expecting it to go down in flames and I’m perfectly content with that

item.title: A Treasure Chest for (media) Pirates
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Comedy

Page Layout (Optional): Normal, but with "Notable Files" log.

Elevator Pitch: An anomaly where filesharing sites and FTP servers spontaneously obtain all pieces of media, even lost media with no evidence for its existence.

Central Narrative: Upon the first manifestation of the anomaly on ftp://[REDACTED], The Foundation, upon discovering mountains of classified material, and world governments, upon discovering mountains of illegal content, collaborate to shut down sites affected by SCP-XXXX. One server is archived by the Foundation, and contains the presumably infinite (yet 100TB in size) archive.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Notable content is recorded on a log by Information Researcher Jones. Throughout the logs, he documents his experiences and how his mental state is affected from seeing some of the more disturbing content in the archive.

Additional Notes: The concept of this is essentially "What if the Foundation was responsible for shutting down so many filesharing sites?".

item.title: Tale about the fall of the SCP Foundation.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Elevator Pitch: The fall of the SCP Foundation is happening. Almost all of the SCPs have breached containment and are roaming the world. Site-[REDACTED] has almost been completely destroyed. The foundation is trying its best to re-contain all of the escaped SCPs

Central Narrative: One of the survivors of the site wide containment breach was a containment specialist, Victor. He was inside of the cafeteria eating his lunch when an unknown group broke into the site and freed almost all of the hostile SCPs. Victor escaped the site.

Now he has to survive in the most intense apocalypse known to mankind.

Hook/Attention Grabber: Its unique because Victor is dealing with many SCPs that have breached containment, and are possibly hostile. He has to survive a long and stressful time.

Additional Notes: I need help with the central narrative and the hook/attention grabber.

item.title: Dissociative Somnia Phenomenon
item.content:encoded:
Seeking greenlight: YES

Page type: SCP Article

Elevator pitch:
An event in which an individual, usually that suffers from night terrors, will experience a dissociative episode(out of body experience) by "dreaming" about dying or killing. The dreams represent with precision the death of a person close to them, who will die within the next few weeks. Attempts to prevent this fate will often result in catastrophic outcomes.

Central Narrative:
The Inevitability of death and acceptance of loss.

Hook:
It's the classic "how would you react if you knew someone that you like is going to die?". I believe this concept to be interesting enough for the small intended size of the article.

Additional notes:
I'm not a hundred percent sure there isn't anything like this on the site already. I've looked around and found nothing that's close, but if there is, please, feel free to warn me.

item.title: The Most Annoying Fly You'll Ever Meet.
item.description: You know that fly that always seems to sneak its way into your room at night? Well, it can be much, much worse.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror with a tinge of dark comedy.

Page Layout (Optional): A standard SCP article included with experiences of D-Class dealing with the SCP and footnotes of some unusual instances of the SCP

Elevator Pitch: The first instance of SCP-??? is a small gnat that appears in the affected individual’s room anywhere from 10 P.M to 2 A.M and is first seen flying around a light source in the room or heard buzzing past the individual’s ear. This gnat proves extremely annoying, being nearly impossible to catch and contain for the night and will buzz by the individual’s ear just as they’re falling asleep. However, the gnat is very easy to kill, seemingly stopping if it’s approached with the intent of swatting it. But, killing the gnat will activate the next “stage” of SCP-???, this time a fly. Killing this instance again “ramps” up the SCP to a mosquito the next night, and so on and so on until you get mosquitoes with malaria, murder hornets, and other terrible crawlies. However, no matter what stage you’re on, they all follow the same rule of the insect being able to fly around and of being easy to kill but nearly impossible to catch and contain.

Central Narrative: I want to focus on how D-Class subjects either cope or go insane from this terrible predicament, and how bad it can get if you keep ramping up the stages.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A crawly in your rooms at night is something we’ve all dealt with at some point, so I feel like that familiar premise combined with my unique (hopefully) idea activates that deep fear of insects in the reader.

Additional Notes: I’m not positive if I want to have it ramp up to the point of being unbearable, or plateau at a certain point so it’s not enough to be completely devastating, but the annoyance is enough to slowly eat away at the individual. Curious on what your thoughts are.

Central Narrative: The heat signature is from a man that when researched can be found on file from [DATA REDACTED], Japan. He doesn’t seem aware that a nuke hit said city and lives in it agelessly

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The man has been shown to be talking to unknown people in the city in trivial conversation. It is unknown whether he is talking to an anomalous affect or is a schizophrenic. Additional Notes: When the man goes to the edges of the city large tremors happen around him. It is unknown if him leaving will result in his neutralization. To counteract this he is forced by the foundation to stay in the inner area of the city until more information is found.

item.title: Of sirens and memetic agents
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, Romance, History

Elevator Pitch: A siren that travels the world's seas in search of someone to marry. She exposes people to auditory and visual memetic agents that will make the exposed person fall in love with her; this usually ends with the siren accidentally drowning the exposed person. Any accurate depiction of her also carries this effect. However, the memes will only work on people who identify as a woman: people who identify as male will have a violent reaction to memes. The memes aren't distributed by artistic interpretations of her.

She first appeared in 1882; she was less of a problem then because she mostly isolated herself in the middle of the Atlantic ocean, not aware of the outside world. However, with the rise of mass media and the internet, she became more of a problem to secrecy as she began patrolling closer to large population centers and started placing advertisements carrying memetic agents on the internet through anomalous and non-anomalous means.

Central Narrative: The foundation originally discovered the siren in 1882, but due to her remote location, the foundation maneuvered ships away from her position and kept her mostly uncontained. The disappearance of Natalie Wood is the first real sign that the Siren has taken more provocative actions to secure a bride. The foundation can get a hold of her and does some interviews:

  • The first goes in-depth about her history: Her familial line is dying off and she was forced into marriage. However, due to her sexuality and her failing relationship with her husband, she ran away from home in search of another bride.
  • The second has the foundation propose an alternative; she can find a bride within the foundation staff as long as she stops advertising on the internet.
  • The third is a list of multiple proposed brides, equipped with memetic dampeners, and the siren's reaction to them. One of them gets selected, and some conversations are logged. It ends on a sweet tone, the siren finally having found someone who likes her back.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's a wholesome article and this is mostly targeted at an audience that likes that, and it's pretty big. It also plays with the siren formula and introduces it to a modern setting. You could see it as a more family-friendly version of the original ''teenage succubus'' SCP.

item.title: SCP: Kingdom Come my first tale
item.description: The book of revelations with SCPs, inspired by DC's Kingdom Come
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

page type tale

genre: horror

page layout a transcript of a conversation with passages from the book revelations used as a framing device

Elevator pitch: Going off of what was established in the tale "new job". A former researcher on his death bed shares visions of an apocalyptic battle between SCP-999 and the scarlet king.

central narrative: while being read his last rites, the dying man interrupts the priest and starts yelling about his visions. The priest tries to tell him to save his strength, but the man insists he must listen. The visions begin with a great war between the SCP foundation and 6 other groups of interests, the war being about weather to destroy anomalies, study them, or let them be. The War comes to a head with an all out seige on site 19, where SCP-988 is being kept. During the battle, SCP-999 supposedly dies to save a researcher from SCP-049. That researcher then finds and opens SCP-988 The visions then skip ahead to the end of the seige, where SCP-053 and 682 are united and release some of the most dangerous SCPs. The survivors of the ensuing chaos come together despite their differences to try and stop this army of SCPs, and the Scarlet king feeds off the chaos of this battle. Pretty soon a portal to the scarlet king's world rips open and fire rains down as the Scarlet king enters our world. Just then SCP-999 reappears with a handful of other thaumiel class SCPs. Unfortunately the man dies before he can tell the man how it ends, but he does leave him with a warning not to "face the light when the day comes" before passing away.

hook: its an end of the world prediction that sorta lines up with the book of revelations.

item.title: The Hypnotic Spider
item.description: A tarantula that’s colors hypnotize any subject to view it. The subject will be compelled to let the tarantula eat it.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch: People are horrified of spiders. This tarantula will grow depending on the amount it consumes. Since its anomalous effect is hypnotizing people to let it eat them, it can be a catastrophe if it ever gets loose.

Central Narrative: Will be about the spider itself and let the reader imagine the implications of the set of conditions for the SCP

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The spider is a Pamphobeteus sp. machala which has a beautifully purple carapace. It’s bright and to assume that looking at this spider will compel you to let it eat you.

Additional Notes: If this spider is ever let loose, it can grow to colossal size and be unstoppable if it finds enough food before teams are able to neutralize it.
